introduced: 46454b8a, 30 September 2026, 'Add bounded source PDF OCR candidate adapter': one page-side check for
the OCR adapter. The commit message states no reason and the line has no comment.
4575b58b, 2 October 2026, 'Support bounded OCR crops on large source pages': a selection may come from
a page up to 14,400 pt a side (line 26) when the selected side is at most 2000 pt (line 126); the
statedReason: The only words are in 4575b58b. Its code comment (lines 114-115): 'Whole-page support is unchanged.
Large source frames are useful only through an explicit, bounded selection; never rasterize them
whole.' Its assignment, docs/orchestration/OCR_LARGE_PLAN_01.md: 'Keep whole-page support at its
existing 2000-point profile', 'Do not just remove checks or globally enlarge whole-page rendering',
and 'Metadata renderSupport currently describes whole-page rendering and may remain unsupported for a
large page; don't relabel it supported merely because cropping works.'
So the limit was set for OCR input. The pages read (d8ba409a, 1 October) borrowed the same check for
its picture (scripts/usp/document-models/run_pdf_pages.py:105-109); no reason for viewing was stated.

listing: 16-19, 36-37): page, label, sourceLabel, frame (kind, rotation, width, height in pt), mediaBox,
cropBox, boxConvention, renderSupport 'supported' | 'unsupported', url (the raster read, or null when
not supported: document-pages.ts:189), locator, calibration null.
No scale, no pixel size and no render profile is stated in the listing.
rasterRead: GET /api/v1/sources/{sourceId}/pages/{page}/raster: the PNG, with headers set in
X-Source-Revision, X-Source-Sha256, X-Document-Page. The scale is stated here, and only here.
The worker's record behind them is DocumentPageRenderSchema (contract lines 20-24), not published.

reads: url and frame. With url null it says the server cannot render the page. With a url it loads the
PNG and stretches it over an SVG whose viewBox is the frame in points, then outlines the region in
points. It reads neither renderSupport nor any header, so a reduced picture is placed correctly
frame, mediaBox, cropBox. None reads renderSupport or url (git grep over packages/server).
whether to give a url, and whether a raster may be published

readers.who: the OCR path and the packet region path
reads: neither the listing's picture fields nor the raster read

guaranteePlanned: _selection and render_pdf_selection keep refusing a whole page over the limit unless the caller passes
an explicit viewing argument; run_pdf_pages.py is the only caller that passes it. The OCR worker, the

why: A reduced picture can be told apart without touching a field another reader depends on: renderSupport
is read only inside document-pages.ts, so a new value 'reduced' (with 'supported' and 'unsupported'
meaning what they mean) plus one optional scale field in the listing is additive for every reader
found above. The scale alone would not tell them apart: Magnolia's reduced 0.587 lies between the
0.7 and 0.6315 that pages within the limit get today.

forTheLeadBeforeTheCode.point: one line outside 'documentation only' in the controller
what: The raster read's only fields are response headers, written in document-pages.controller.ts. To
state 'reduced' there (the scale is already in X-Page-Pixel-Affine) one header line is needed in
that file, which K9e owns for documentation only. Planned as one header line plus its
documentation, named in the report; say if it should be left out.

forTheLeadBeforeTheCode.point: the frozen region profile lists run_pdf_pages.py
what: usp/packets/region-runtime.ts:13-16 and packet_region_loader.py:17-21 pin run_pdf_pages.py among the
region runtime's files. Changing it means the region read answers PACKET_REGION_EXECUTABLE_DRIFT
until the profile is rebuilt, which docs/backend/DEMO-RUNTIME.md step 5 already orders at every
roll. Nothing for this task to run; for the runtime owner to know.
